title: Suite run blind: the routine's prod CLI session expired after 7 days and nothing could renew it
service: echopoint-investigation routine (prod-org flow suites on dev)
summary: The 23:08Z run of the scheduled flow-suite routine checked no flow: both `flows run --tag` calls exited 1 with `stored credentials have expired`. The routine's `prod` CLI profile held only a browser session, a JWT with a fixed 7-day life and no refresh token, signed in on 2026-10-19T20:21Z; it expired at 2026-10-26T20:21Z. Nothing warned before expiry, the CLI never falls back to a stored API key once a session expired, and the routine cannot sign in by itself. Post-deploy gates and the Daily schedule were unaffected (they use their own credentials), and no backend change merged in the window. The suite runner now checks the credential before launching; a CLI fallback awaits review; a human must store a CI-org API key to end the class.

impact.text: One routine run (of four a day) checked 0 of 66 flows; coverage of new dev merges stays blind until a human signs in again. Customers saw nothing: the flows only target dev, and the gates and Daily schedule run with separate credentials.

trigger: The `prod` profile's session JWT reached its `exp` at 2026-10-26T20:21:26Z.
detection: The next scheduled run (23:08Z) saw both suite launches exit 1 within a second; `anchor.log` and `echopoint.log` held `stored credentials have expired`. The expiry date had been visible in `echopoint auth status` for 7 days, but nothing read it.
resolution: Not resolved by the routine: re-authentication needs a person at a browser, and the routine never enters credentials. `run_suites.sh` now stops with `AUTH-EXPIRED` and warns `AUTH-EXPIRES-SOON` 48 h ahead; a CLI change lets a stored API key replace an expired session.

events.label: Prod CLI profile signed in by browser (7-day JWT)
events.detail: `exp` minus 7 days; the login is also noted in the routine's Run notes (credential written without `organization_id`).

events.label: Last green suite run ends (anchor 27/27, echopoint 39/39)
Session JWT expires
events.detail: `~/.echopoint/credentials/prod.json` `expires_at` 2026-10-26T16:21:26-04:00, keys `access_token`, `expires_at`, `organization_id`: no refresh token, no API key.

events.label: Both suite tags exit 1: credentials expired
events.detail: `run_suites.sh` output `anchor: exit 1 pass 0 fail 0`, `echopoint: exit 1 pass 0 fail 0`.

events.label: Preflight added: AUTH-EXPIRED / AUTH-EXPIRES-SOON
events.detail: The runner now stops with an actionable line and warns 48 h before the next expiry.

events.label: Impact bounded: run reported, human sign-in requested
events.detail: Suites stay blind until a person signs in or stores an API key (action A1).

whys.problem: The 23:08Z routine run checked no flow, so a dev regression merged now would go unseen

because.text: Every `flows run --profile prod` exited 1 with `stored credentials have expired` before launching
The prod profile held only a browser session: a JWT with a fixed 7-day `exp` and no refresh token
The routine runs unattended four times a day but signs in as a person, the way an interactive user does
No non-expiring credential (a CI-org API key) is set up for unattended suite runs on the routine host
A stored API key would not have helped: the CLI fails on an expired session before it looks at a stored key
because.evidence: `resolveToken` returns the expiry error before `resolveStoredAPIKey` (`internal/commands/root.go`); `echopoint mcp` already falls back (`mcp.go`)

because.text: CLI command auth treats an expired session as fatal even when a stored (or preferred) API key exists
Nobody knew ahead: the expiry date sat in `auth status` for 7 days and the run found out only after the fact
`run_suites.sh` launched the suites without reading the credential
The suite runner had no credential preflight and no warning before expiry
Recovery waits for a person: the routine cannot sign in by itself and must not handle passwords
Browser sign-in is the only credential the host holds, and it needs a person at a browser
The routine has no credential path it can renew without a person (same gap as R1)

contributing: The `dev` profile (used by the `echopoint_dev` MCP) is a browser session too and expires at 2026-10-27T03:03Z.
The 2026-10-19 sign-in already broke one run (missing `organization_id`); that fix pinned the org but did not question the credential type.

well: The CLI error named the cause and the fix, so diagnosis took one command.
Gates and the Daily schedule use separate credentials, so prod promotion checks were unaffected.
wrong: A known expiry date went unread for 7 days.
The CLI's fallback to a stored API key works in `echopoint mcp` but not in commands, so the obvious mitigation would also have failed.
lucky: No echopoint, anchor, runner or CLI change merged during the blind window.
The expiry hit between runs, not during one: a mid-run expiry would have left half-run flows and leaked cleanup.

actions.what: Create a CI-org API key for the routine and store it on the host with `echopoint auth login --profile prod --api-key <key> --default` (and the same for `dev` if the dev MCP must stay up); sign in again meanwhile
CLI commands fall back to a stored API key when the session expired, like `echopoint mcp`
`run_suites.sh` preflight: stop with `AUTH-EXPIRED`, warn `AUTH-EXPIRES-SOON` 48 h ahead, skip when an API key is preferred
flow-suite-testing skill: an unattended run signs in with an org API key and checks it before launching

messaging.internal: Flow suites did not run at 23:08Z: the routine's prod CLI session expired (7-day browser JWT). Please sign in again, ideally store a CI-org API key with `--default`. Gates and Daily are unaffected.
